newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sappi sees better second half.
newsitem.headline: Sappi sees better second half.

text.p: South African pulp and paper producer Sappi Ltd said on Monday that pulp demand in recent months had been strong, but prices were at a low level.
However, the firm, which earlier announced a slide in half year earnings to 16 cents from 215 last time, said the second half of the the current year is likely to see a pick up.
"Producer stocks have shown a decline in recent months and price increases have been announced by most of the major suppliers effective May, 1997," the firm said in a statement.
Sappi said the price increases seemed to have been accepted by the market.

The firm said that North America was looking like it would be at the crest of the recovery, as paper consumption and demand looked especially healthy in the region and prices there were now showing an upward trend.

"In Europe, however, currency fluctuations and new coated paper capacity have stemmed the rate of price increases, but rising pulp prices should support the current or better levels to the balance of the year," the firm said.

Analysts had expected a dismal set of results from Sappi as the rock bottom prices in the industry bit into its earnings. They had forecast earnings in a range of 10 to 40 cents with the consensus figure coming in at 27.5 cents.
Sappi scrapped its dividend for the period, a move that some analysts had predicted.
